title: La masa del sábado
desc: Saturday night, fifty nacatamales, and an arm that stops working
setting: It is nine at night, doña Chepa's kitchen is full of steam, and somebody has handed you a wooden spoon.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Venga, mijo. Batí esa masa un rato que a mí ya se me murió el brazo.
steps.en: Come here, love. Beat that dough a while, my arm is dead already.

options.es: Deme acá, doña. ¿Hasta cuándo la bato?
options.en: Give it here, doña. How long do I beat it for?
options.feedback: Take it and ask how you will know when it is done. The answer is by hand and by look, which is why she has to show you.

options.en: I do not know how to do that.
options.feedback: Nobody is asking you to know. You are being asked because there are fifty of these to make before morning.

options.en: And is there no machine for it?
options.feedback: There is, and hers is by hand, and that is the reason people buy hers. Say that in that kitchen and see how it lands.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Hasta que quede suave. Maíz molido, manteca y sal, nada más.
steps.en: Until it goes smooth. Ground maize, lard and salt, nothing else.

options.es: ¿Y por qué solo los domingos, doña?
options.en: And why only on Sundays, doña?
options.feedback: The right question while your arm is busy. A nacatamal is Sunday-morning food and nobody makes one on a Wednesday.
You are working, which is what the kitchen needs. She is in a talking mood and you are not using it.

options.es: Esto lleva un montón de trabajo.
options.en: This is an awful lot of work.
options.feedback: The work is the entire reason it means something. Say that in that kitchen and watch her face.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Porque es comida de domingo, pues. Y porque una no puede todos los días.
steps.en: Because it is Sunday food. And because a woman cannot do this every day.

options.es: Con razón la cuadra huele igual los domingos.
options.en: No wonder the whole block smells the same on Sundays.
options.feedback: You put two things together out loud. Three houses on this street are doing exactly this tonight and by nine tomorrow the smell is the same in all of them.
Fair. There was a better sentence in you about the smell of the street.

options.es: Podría hacerlos entre semana y vender más.
options.en: You could make them midweek and sell more.
options.feedback: Nobody would buy one. Advising a woman of sixty on her own business is a fast way to be handed back the spoon.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mañana a las siete le guardo uno. Con su pedazo de cerdo.
steps.en: Tomorrow at seven I will keep one for you. With its piece of pork.

options.es: Ahí estoy a las siete, doña. Con gaseosa roja.
options.en: I will be there at seven, doña. With a red fizzy drink.
options.feedback: Seven in the morning, and the red gaseosa beside it. You have just described a Nicaraguan Sunday exactly as it is.

options.en: Thank you, doña. I will be there.
options.feedback: Fine. Naming the hour tells her you know it will be gone by nine.

options.es: ¿Me lo puede guardar para el mediodía?
options.en: Could you keep it for me until midday?
options.feedback: By midday there are none left anywhere in the barrio. That is the one rule of the nacatamal.
